head: 658ed6a5808b8e2f3b82f419050354c73c4ebd4e
summary:
I re-validated HEAD 658ed6a against the real C:\ drive, using a freshly published exe and the project's own Core. At the default 880x600 window, O-024 is fixed. With the unreadable-folders list opened by the project's hook (expand mode) on a real C:\ scan (3,586,901 files, 663 unreadable folders), LargestFilesList is 63.47 px and inView with 5 rows built, and UnreadableList is 53.23 px and inView. largestFilesMs was 36.90 ms, under the 100 ms threshold O-021 set.

This time I also checked every row of the real list, not just row 0. I ran the project's own Scanner.Scan and LargestFiles.Top on C:\ in a throwaway harness. All 100 rows exist at the path shown, and each logical size equals the file system's. On-disk equals the file's allocation for every row: 98 match cluster rounding and two over-allocated files match a direct AllocationSize read. The two rows that could not be opened are pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys (ProbeFailed); their logical sizes match and their on-disk values are cluster-aligned. A separate walk found only two files at least as large as the cut that are missing from the list, and both are later hardlink names.

Criterion 14 is now checked on real data. 98 rows are SizeProbed and 2 are ProbeFailed. The store holds 195,356 online-only files, 36 of them logically larger than the cut, and none is listed, as ranking by on-disk space intends.

Other checks at this HEAD pass: xUnit 166/166, Fitness 26/26, rules-parity AGREE, WindowCases -Case All 21/21 (L-003 opened: 95.8 px and 74.8 px, both inView), and HookCases H-001/H-002. My first HookCases call failed only because I left out -Case.

What does not hold: the fit only holds at the default size, and I measured that on this drive. At 880x560 with the list opened, both lists are clipped at their MinHeight of 40, so neither is inView. At the window's own minimum of 560x400, nothing below the outcome texts is on screen, with the unreadable-folders list open or closed. The texts alone overflow the panel there, and that was already true before this slice (at uat the unreadable-folders expander filled the space below the same texts). With the list opened at the default size there is only about 30 px to spare. The design, L-003, O-024 and the earlier revoke all judge criterion 11 at the default size, so I grade it met there and record the smaller sizes as failed checks. A later slice needs to decide what window size the outcome panel must support.

Ledger: build-slice attempts 4 to 36 were provider refusals that changed nothing (code review already named that loop), and attempt 3 is marked passed at 658ed6a even though its summary is a refusal. The real work is attempt 37.

I changed nothing in the tree. The throwaway hooks, the harness and the logs in %TEMP% have been deleted.

Rows 96-99 tie at 811,556,864 on disk, and no other non-duplicate file of that size was left out.

Store: 263,815 SizeProbed, 7 ProbeFailed (2 of them at or above the cut, both listed), 195,356 CloudOnly (36 of them with logical size at or above the cut, none listed, because they are ranked by on-disk bytes, about 0).

criteria.criterion: 1. rank the largest files under the scanned root (top level and six folders down; a folder's total larger than any file)
criteria.how: RanksFilesAtAnyDepthAndNeverAFolder passes at HEAD (166/166). On real C:\ the list holds files at depths from 1 (pagefile.sys) to 8 or more (huggingface blobs, docker_data.vhdx). Top keeps Kind==File only, and every row exists as a file.

criteria.criterion: 2. cap the list at count (105 files, count 100, ties at the cut)
criteria.how: KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut and L-003 ('Top 100 of 105') pass. On real C:\ there are exactly 100 rows, and rows 96-99 tie at 811,556,864. The independent walk found no other non-duplicate file at or above the cut left out.

criteria.criterion: 3. list a tree that has nothing to rank
criteria.how: ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList and L-004 ('No non-empty files found.', 0 rows, largestFileOnDisk null) pass at HEAD.

criteria.criterion: 4. list a file that has more than one name
criteria.how: AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce passes. On real C:\ the only two files at or above the cut missing from the list are later hardlink names (HardlinkDuplicate), so each hardlinked file appears once.
NoRowComesFromALink (real file symlink, folder symlink and junction, never skipped) passes. On real C:\, 20,458 links were not followed, and every row is a real file at its own path.

criteria.criterion: 6. rank by space on disk with both sizes shown
criteria.how: RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes passes, and the XAML shows 'On disk' and 'Size' under 'Largest files, by space on disk'. On real C:\ both values are exact per row, for example the ollama blob with 4,676,845,568 on disk against 4,676,804,928 logical, confirmed by an independent AllocationSize read.

criteria.criterion: 7. show where a file is (>260 chars, trailing dot, trailing space, unpaired surrogate)
criteria.how: EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath passes. L-003 draws the surrogate row 0 with the list both closed and opened, and the exe exits 0. On real C:\ all 100 shown paths resolve to existing files through \\?\, including names with spaces, commas and apostrophes. No person looked at the rendering.

criteria.criterion: 8. list from a scan that was stopped
criteria.how: AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead and L-005 (Cancelled, partial list, '... before the scan stopped.' caption) pass at HEAD. Core is unchanged since ef74cd1, so O-001's reading of Scanner.cs still holds.

criteria.criterion: 9. start another scan after a list has been shown
criteria.how: L-006 passes in both shapes on the new Grid layout: the list collapses with 0 rows at the start of the second scan, and at its failure ending.

criteria.criterion: 10. state what the list does not cover
criteria.how: L-002 passes. On real C:\ the caption reads 'Top 100 of 35,86,901 files scanned. Files in 663 unreadable folders are not included.'

criteria.criterion: 11. fit the list into the outcome panel (100 rows, surrogate row, unreadable list also filled)
criteria.how: Met at the default 880x600, the size the design, L-003, O-024 and the revoke judge against. On real C:\ with 663 unreadable folders and the list opened, LargestFilesList is 63.47 px inView (5 rows built) and UnreadableList is 53.23 px inView. L-003 passes closed (226 px, 7 of 100 built) and opened (95.8 and 74.8 px). It does NOT hold at smaller window sizes the app allows. At 880x560 opened, both lists are clipped at MinHeight 40. At 560x400, open or closed, nothing below the outcome texts is on screen. That overflow predates this slice (the same texts overflow the panel), and the opened state has about 30 px to spare at the default size. See the failed checks.

criteria.criterion: 12. report what the window shows after a finished scan of a planted tree
criteria.how: L-001 passes. The real C:\ reports carry every key, including the new UnreadableExpander.expanded and UnreadableList{actualHeight,inView}, with sane values and no paths.

criteria.criterion: 13. rank a very large scan (4-5 million entries)
criteria.how: Real C:\ store of 4,435,838 entries: largestFilesMs was 36.90 ms in the default-size run, 31.18 to 36.51 ms in three runs alongside other scans, and Top took 39.67 ms in the Core harness. All are under the 100 ms Task.Run threshold (O-021). LargestFilesScaleTests passes.

criteria.criterion: 14. rank a file whose size the scanner had to probe (open and growing, probe failed, online-only placeholder)
criteria.how: On the real C:\ list, 98 rows are SizeProbed and 2 are ProbeFailed (pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys). Every row's logical size matches the file system, and every probed row's on-disk value matches its allocation. The 195,356 online-only files, 36 of them logically larger than the cut, are absent because they take about 0 on disk, as the design's ranking intends. An open-and-growing file was not specifically identified on the list; the spike covers that shape. This was checked through Core's LargestFiles.Top, the call the App makes; the window shows no per-row flags.

obligations.evidence: At HEAD 658ed6a the outcome panel is a Grid of rows Auto / 3* / (Auto, or 2* while the list is opened and visible) (MainWindow.xaml:39-70). On the real C:\ drive at the default 880x600 with the list opened by the project's expand hook, LargestFilesList is 63.47 px inView and UnreadableList 53.23 px inView. At validate attempt 1 the same scenario gave 0 px and inView false. The fix is bounded: at 880x560 opened, both lists are clipped at MinHeight 40, and at 560x400 the pre-existing texts overflow hides both lists whether the list is open or closed.

Unchanged since it was discharged: git diff ef74cd1..HEAD -- src/FsAnalyser.Core is empty, so the single-threaded Scanner.Scan and the join in SynchronousIoCancel.Dispose that I read at attempt 1 are the code under test.

not_reached: What window size the outcome panel must support is undecided. The design names none, and the window allows 560x400. Below the default, the list is clipped (880x560 opened) or entirely off screen (560x400 open or closed, where the pre-existing outcome texts already overflow). With the list opened at the default size there is about 30 px to spare, so a drive with more outcome notes, or a larger system text size, could clip it at the default size too. Neither was measured.

The completeness walk under OneDrive was refused by the guard. The independent walk also skipped cloud-reparse folders, so completeness was checked only across the roughly 2.6M files outside them. Online-only files were seen only through the scanner's own CloudOnly flags.
An open-and-growing file was not identified as a row on the real list. That shape rests on the spike open-growing-file-stale-directory-size.
The on-disk sizes of pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys could not be read independently unelevated (open fails). Only their logical sizes were compared. The spike matched pagefile.sys to CIM.
No person looked at the window. Row rendering (wrapped long paths, the lone-surrogate name, the column alignment) was judged only from report metrics.
The contents of the 663 unreadable folders on C:\: the list cannot include them. read-denied-folders returns counts only, so it could not show whether a larger file is there.
Windows 10, non-100% DPI and text scaling, and drives other than NTFS C:\ (exFAT/FAT removable media, a mapped SMB share) with the list shown.
